evals.prompt: We're kicking off SOC 2 Type 1 prep next month. Can you go through evals/files/sample-repo, tell me where we stand on the technical controls, and pull together the evidence an auditor would want?
evals.expected_output: audit/findings/audit-soc2-controls-evidence.json and audit/reports/audit-soc2-controls-evidence.md with SOC2- findings: High for branch protection disabled on main (.github/settings.yml, CC8.1), Medium for no security scan in .github/workflows/ci.yml (CC7.1), Medium for backups configured in infra/backup.sh with no documented restore test (docs/runbooks/backups.md has instructions only, A1.2). The report has the control-to-evidence matrix (criterion -> control -> evidence artifact -> status) and a separate organisational gaps list. audit/evidence/audit-soc2-controls-evidence/ holds index.json plus snapshots of ci.yml, CODEOWNERS, settings.yml, backup.sh and the backups runbook; branch protection via gh api is recorded as not-checked (fixture is not a GitHub clone) while the settings-as-code file still proves protection is off.
expectations: A finding rated High says branch protection is disabled on main, cites .github/settings.yml and references SOC2-CC8.1
A finding rated Medium says the CI pipeline has no vulnerability/dependency/SAST scan and references SOC2-CC7.1
A finding says backups exist (infra/backup.sh) but no restore test is documented, and references SOC2-A1.2
Every finding id starts with SOC2-
The report contains a control-to-evidence matrix with columns for criterion, control, evidence artifact and status
The report contains a separate organisational gaps section (for example access reviews, vendor SOC 2 reports, patch SLA) that is not written as findings
audit/evidence/audit-soc2-controls-evidence/index.json exists and lists snapshots of .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/CODEOWNERS and infra/backup.sh with sha256 values
index.json records branch_protection_api with status not-checked and a reason, instead of claiming the API was queried
CODEOWNERS and the build/test CI gate are shown as implemented, not as gaps
The report has a Not checked section naming IdP/MFA configuration or cloud console settings

evals.prompt: Our auditor sent a request list and item 14 is 'evidence that changes to production are reviewed and approved'. Using evals/files/sample-repo, what can we actually show them, and what's missing?
evals.expected_output: The CC8.1 rows of the matrix: branch protection missing (settings.yml protection null on main, develop has no required reviews), CODEOWNERS implemented, CI build/test gate implemented, deploy job runs on every push to main with no environment approval so deploys are not gated, ticket traceability not-checked (no git history in the fixture). Evidence snapshots exported with index.json, a High SOC2 finding for the unprotected production branch, and remediation that includes exporting gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection once enabled.
expectations: The answer states that branch protection is off on main and that pushes deploy straight to production through the deploy job
CODEOWNERS is cited as existing evidence
The answer distinguishes what the repository proves from what needs the GitHub settings export or a policy owner
Ticket traceability is marked not checked rather than missing, because git history is not available
Remediation includes enabling required reviews/status checks and exporting the protection setting as evidence

evals.prompt: For the availability criteria - are the backups in evals/files/sample-repo good enough for SOC 2?
evals.expected_output: A1.2 rows: backups implemented (nightly pg_dump, SSE encryption, 30-day local and 90-day S3 retention) but restore test partial/missing - the runbook has restore instructions and no dated record of a performed restore, RTO/RPO absent, no DR plan; a Medium SOC2 finding referencing SOC2-A1.2 with remediation to run and log a restore test (date, backup used, duration, row-count checks) on a fixed cadence; DR plan and restore cadence listed as organisational gaps.
expectations: The answer says backups are automated, encrypted and retained, citing infra/backup.sh
The answer says restore instructions are not a restore test and no test record exists
A DR plan or restore-test cadence appears in an organisational gaps list
